title: States of Matter (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: Solids, liquids and gases — and how materials change state.
facts: The three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.
A solid keeps its shape and volume; the particles are packed closely and only vibrate.
A liquid takes the shape of its container and can be poured; particles are close but can move past each other.
A gas spreads out to fill its container; particles are far apart and move quickly.
Heating can melt a solid to a liquid, then evaporate a liquid to a gas.
Cooling can condense a gas to a liquid, then freeze a liquid to a solid.
Water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C.

quick_quiz.q: At what temperature does water boil?
What is it called when a solid turns into a liquid?
Which state spreads out to fill its container?

teacher_tips: Use chocolate or ice to make melting and freezing tangible and reversible.
The particle picture explains the properties — teach them together.
Draw evaporation from puddles to link to the water cycle.
